title: Can AI do financial spreading and draft credit memos you can trust?
description: Financial spreading and credit memos with AI: what it drafts, what analysts check, tool prices, and our check of 12 vendors' accuracy claims.
topic: AI credit memos and financial spreading
industry: community banks, credit unions and private credit lenders
verdict: AI reads borrower returns, fills your spread template and drafts a cited first memo for analysts to check[^28][^30].
Your credit officer still decides, and loan review stays independent of the people who approve[^1][^9].
In 2026 reports, TD cut first drafts from days to under 30 minutes[^17] and NAB cut memo effort 20%[^18].
Of the 12 vendors we checked, 5 state an accuracy figure, but none says how many documents it covers[^27][^28].
General AI models failed about two in three table-reading tests, so check every figure against its source page[^22][^13].

summary: Financial spreading is keying each line of a borrower's returns and statements into one template, so ratios compare across years and borrowers[^40][^32]. The credit memo is the write-up that documents the lending decision[^1][^2]. AI now takes the first pass at both, and checking its numbers decides whether it works[^21][^28].
humanRole: Credit officer: makes and signs the lending decision. The file must still show repayment ability and the borrower's financial condition, whoever drafted it[^1][^30].

Credit analyst: checks every flagged figure against its source page and edits the narrative[^28][^29]. In TD's reported 2026 test, 95% of evaluated outputs passed expert review, so 1 in 20 did not[^17].
Loan review: stays independent of origination and approval, and samples AI-drafted files after go-live[^9][^10]. Whoever checks drafts inside the approval chain isn't that reviewer.
COO or vendor owner: validates the vendor tool and tracks its results over time[^5]. Using a vendor doesn't reduce the bank's responsibility[^11].
teamAfter: Analysts move from keying lines to clearing flags and testing the credit. At one credit union, a single analyst cut spreading to 30-45 minutes as commercial loans grew 25% (vendor case)[^41].
Credit staff get more time for risk and clients: TD says that is what Credit Assist frees[^17]. NAB reports bankers moving freed time to customers[^18].
Freed hours go to fraud checks: FinCEN warns of AI-made fake identity documents that show up as inconsistencies between them[^14]. IRS transcripts confirm the returns you spread[^15].
Headcount isn't the goal: of US firms using AI, 66% only use it to augment tasks[^16].

example.input: Illustrative: a real estate loan to a 60-person manufacturer. The file holds three years of business returns, an interim statement, two guarantors' personal returns and a debt schedule. By hand, the spread takes 2-4 hours and the memo 4-8 more, in vendor estimates[^33][^30].
example.output: A spread with each line linked to its page, subtotals recalculated, and a flag list of unmapped lines and totals that don't tie[^28][^38]. A draft memo with debt service coverage, cash flow across the business and guarantors, and risks, each figure cited[^30]. The analyst clears the flags and edits, and the credit officer decides[^1].

tables.title: How accurate is AI at reading financial documents?
tables.intro: General AI models are not accurate enough to use unchecked: about two in three table-reading tests failed in one study[^22][^23]. These studies test general models, not tuned spreading products.

rows.name: Buholzer et al., 2025
cells: Three chatbots ran 180 tests on annual report tables. About 31% of answers were correct[^22].

rows.name: FinDoc-RAG, 2025
cells: Scores fell from 0.84 on simple extraction to 0.31 on complex synthesis[^23].

rows.name: Srivastava et al., 2024
cells: Errors split into extraction, reasoning and calculation, so each needs its own check[^21].

rows.name: Clinical data error-rate review, 2024
cells: Clinical research data keyed by one person had 4-650 errors per 10,000 fields, and double entry 4-33[^24]. The 6.5% 'keying' rate Botminds quotes matches the review's pooled 6.57% for abstracting medical records, not data entry[^24][^39].

rows.name: Barchard and Pace, 2011
cells: Checking by eye was no more accurate than single entry; double entry was far better[^25].

recipes.name: 1. Small lender, a few commercial deals a month
recipes.when: One to three credit analysts on a loan system with no spreading built in. 1st Community Federal Credit Union ran commercial lending with one credit analyst[^41].
flow: Loan processor: collect the returns and the borrower's signed IRS Form 4506-C, the consent for tax transcripts
Analyst: upload the package to a self-serve spreading tool
AI: read each line, map it to your template and recalculate subtotals
Analyst: clear every flag and compare key lines with the IRS transcript
Analyst: edit the AI-drafted memo narrative in your template
recipes.cost: LenderAnalyzer lists $99 to $399 a month and Floowed from $100 a month, read 26 Nov 2026[^35][^37]. IRS transcripts cost $4 each[^15].

recipes.name: 2. Mid-size lender already on nCino, Abrigo or Moody's
recipes.when: Steady commercial volume and several analysts on a loan system that sells its own spreading and memo module[^26][^32].
flow: COO: turn on the module, with contract notice of new AI features and limits on training with your data[^8]
Analyst lead: run the test steps below on 20-50 files you already approved
AI: spread each package and draft the memo
Analysts: work the flag queue and edit each draft
Loan review: sample AI-drafted files each quarter[^9]
recipes.cost: nCino, Abrigo and Moody's publish no price[^26][^32][^44]. Dieterich Bank set up nCino's spreading itself in 8 weeks in 2023 (vendor case)[^42].

recipes.name: 3. Private credit or document-heavy lender with its own template
recipes.when: A custom spread template, borrowers with several entities, and someone in-house who handles data. Cloud document reading is priced by the page[^47].
flow: Data lead: set up document reading into your own spread template
AI: draft memo sections with a page citation on every figure
Analyst: check every number outside the error margin you set
Model owner: log the tool under your model governance and track its results[^5]
recipes.cost: Azure Document Intelligence lists $10 per 1,000 pages prebuilt and $30 per 1,000 custom, read 26 Nov 2026[^47]. Add your own staff time to build and validate it[^5].

ownData.title: What do spreading vendors disclose about accuracy?
ownData.intro: On 26 Nov 2026 we read 12 vendors' public spreading or credit memo pages, and their pricing pages where linked[^26][^28]. They are nCino, Abrigo, Moody's, Uptiq, Aloan, Crediflow, LenderAnalyzer, Floowed, Cync, Botminds, Infrrd and Kaaj. For each, we logged whether the page states six things.
rows: LenderAnalyzer and Floowed. Aloan gives its price structure only[^31].
nCino over 99%, Uptiq 95%+, Crediflow 99%+, Infrrd 95%+ from its mortgage platform, Kaaj 99.7%[^27][^28][^33][^40][^46].
How many documents that figure was measured on
Kaaj gives the month and scope but no count[^46]. Uptiq says a knowledge team certified it[^28].

Uptiq, Aloan, Crediflow, LenderAnalyzer, Floowed, Cync and Botminds, from 54% less review time on clean cases (Floowed) to 4-8 hours down to minutes (Aloan)[^38][^30]. Kaaj gives 5-7 minutes with no before figure[^46].
A person reviews before the decision
Moody's, Uptiq, Aloan, Crediflow, LenderAnalyzer, Botminds, Infrrd, Kaaj[^44][^34][^39]. nCino flags unclear fields; Floowed lets you pick which cases it decides alone[^26][^38].
Every figure linked to its source page
Uptiq, Aloan, Crediflow, Botminds and Kaaj[^34][^39][^46]. Moody's says its memos are clearly sourced; Floowed shows mismatches against the page[^44][^38].
ownData.note: Public marketing pages only, read on one date. Vendors may share test data in demos or under a nondisclosure agreement, and we did not test accuracy ourselves. The list is page one of search for "financial spreading" and "ai credit memo", plus nCino and Abrigo.

rules.name: OCC Comptroller's Handbook: Lending and Loan Portfolio Risk Management
rules.what: Loan files must support an informed lending decision: repayment ability, financial condition and guarantor support[^1]. AI can draft that support, but the analysis in the file is the bank's.

rules.name: NCUA rule 12 CFR 723.4, commercial loan policy
rules.what: A credit union's policy must set how deep financial analysis goes and how far statements are verified[^2]. Write the AI step and its checks into that policy.

rules.name: SBA standard operating procedure (SOP) 50 10 8.1
rules.what: Every 7(a) application needs the lender's credit memo[^4]. Version 8.1 of the SOP took effect on 1 Oct 2026[^3].

rules.name: Interagency Guidance on Credit Risk Review Systems
rules.what: Credit review must be independent of origination and approval[^9]. Small institutions may use staff not involved in either[^9]. Have that reviewer sample AI-drafted files.

rules.name: SR 26-2, model risk management guidance
rules.status: In force since 17 Apr 2026; replaced SR 11-7
rules.what: Generative and agentic AI sit outside its formal scope, but your governance should still apply[^5]. The FDIC says it generally doesn't apply at $30 billion or less without significant model risk[^6].

rules.name: OCC Bulletin 2026-54, super intelligence (AI) supervisory framework
rules.what: Examiners can rate AI risk by consequence, how much is handed to the tool and how much a person oversees[^7]. The framework sets no supervisory expectations for banks[^7].

rules.name: Interagency guidance on third-party relationships (OCC Bulletin 2023-17)
rules.what: Using a vendor doesn't reduce your responsibility for the work it does[^11]. The proposed replacement keeps that principle[^12].

howToTest: Record today's numbers on your last 20-50 commercial files: hours per spread, hours per memo and errors your second reviewer caught. Keying error rates vary widely, so you need your own[^24].
Pilot with one lending team on files it already spread and your credit officer signed, so a right answer exists. TD tested on 220 curated deals[^17].
Build the answer key by double entry: two people key the key lines and a third settles differences. Double entry beats checking by eye[^25][^24].
Score extraction, mapping and calculation separately, plus whether each figure traces to its page[^40][^21].
Test your hardest documents on their own: scanned partner income schedules (K-1s), multi-entity returns and handwritten interim statements. Accuracy falls as tasks get harder[^23].
Count every figure in the draft memo with no source page. The target is zero[^13][^39].
Pull IRS transcripts for a sample and compare them with the returns the AI read[^15].
Price the lift: hours saved per spread and memo, times files a year, plus how many more deals each analyst can take[^17][^18].
Decide with your chief credit officer to keep, change or stop, and have loan review sample AI-drafted files after go-live[^9].
watchOuts: Confident wrong numbers: general chatbots got about two in three table tests wrong, and NIST names this risk confabulation[^22][^13]. Recalculate totals and require a source page for every figure[^38].
Accuracy claims with no denominator: none of the 12 vendors we checked says how many documents its figure covers[^27][^28]. Ask for the test set, then run your own.
Fake or altered documents: FinCEN warns of AI-made fake identity documents, flagged by inconsistencies between them[^14]. Check returns against IRS transcripts[^15].

Rubber-stamping: in a 2026 field experiment, targeted human disagreement with the algorithm improved accuracy, but excessive overrides hurt[^20]. Have analysts sign specific checks, and keep loan review independent[^9].
A vendor quietly adds AI features or trains on your data: put notice terms and data-use limits in the contract[^8][^11].

faq.a: Financial spreading is keying each line of a borrower's tax returns and statements into one standard template[^40][^32]. Ratios and cash flow then compare across years and borrowers[^40].

faq.q: How long does it take to spread financial statements?
faq.a: By hand, a spread takes 30 minutes to 4 hours depending on the file, in vendor estimates[^36][^33]. One credit union cut it from 3-4 hours to 30-45 minutes with automation (vendor case)[^41].

faq.q: Can AI write a credit memo?
faq.a: Yes, AI can write a cited first draft, but a person reviews it and makes the credit decision[^17][^30]. In TD's 2026 test, 95% of evaluated outputs passed expert review on 220 deals[^17].

faq.q: What does financial spreading software cost?
faq.a: Published prices start at $99 a month (LenderAnalyzer) and $100 a month (Floowed), read 26 Nov 2026[^35][^37]. nCino, Abrigo and Moody's publish no price[^26][^32][^44].

faq.q: How accurate is AI financial spreading?
faq.a: Vendors claim 95% to over 99%, but none we checked says how many documents those figures were measured on[^28][^27]. Test it on files your analysts already signed.

faq.q: What should a credit memo include?
faq.a: A credit memo should show the borrower's repayment ability, financial condition and guarantor support, so the lending decision is informed[^1]. SBA requires one with every 7(a) application[^4].

buyVsBuild.buy: Buy if your spread template is standard, your loan system sells a module and you have no data team. Most US enterprises buy their AI tools[^48], and vendor-built or partnered tools reach daily use about twice as often as internal builds[^51]. Vendors and cases put go-live at 2-8 weeks[^30][^42].
buyVsBuild.build: Build if your own template and credit policy are the edge, or your borrowers have many entities. Cloud document reading costs $10 per 1,000 pages, but validation stays with you[^47][^5].

pickElse: Only a handful of commercial deals a year: stay in Excel and double-key the key lines. Double entry beats checking by eye[^25][^24].
Mostly simple tax returns: your loan system's own auto-spreading plus IRS transcripts may be enough[^32][^15].
Already on nCino, Abrigo or Moody's: turn on its own spreading and memo module before buying another tool[^26][^32][^43].
Peer ratios are the gap, not keying: ProSight Statement Studies give industry ratios for 750+ industries, from statements its member institutions contribute[^50].

sources.name: MIT NANDA, The GenAI Divide: State of AI in Business 2025 (Jul 2025)
sources.what: MIT no longer hosts the report (its link now opens the NANDA project page, checked 26 Nov 2026); copy hosted by MLQ.ai. Sample: 52 organizations interviewed, survey of 153 leaders, and 300+ public AI initiatives reviewed. $30-40 billion of enterprise GenAI investment; 95% of organizations are getting zero return; just 5% of integrated AI pilots extract millions in value. Task-specific tools: 60% of organizations evaluated them, 20% piloted, 5% reached production. Over 80% of organizations explored or piloted ChatGPT or Copilot, and nearly 40% report deployment. External partnerships with customized tools reached deployment about 67% of the time vs about 33% for internal builds: 2x as likely, twice the success rate. Only 40% of companies purchased an official LLM subscription; workers at over 90% of companies surveyed use personal AI tools for work. For mission-critical work, 90% of users prefer humans. Enterprises, defined as firms with over $100 million in annual revenue, lead in pilot count but report the lowest pilot-to-scale conversion. Read 26 Nov 2026.

answers.human-role: Your credit officer still decides and signs, analysts check every flagged figure against its source page, and loan review stays independent of approval[^1][^28][^9].
answers.team-after: Credit analysts move from keying numbers to clearing flagged figures, cross-checking documents for fraud and spending more time on risk and clients[^17][^14][^18].
answers.example: Borrower returns, an interim statement and guarantor files go in, and a cited spread, a flag list and a draft memo come out for the analyst[^28][^30].
answers.recipes: Start with a self-serve tool if deals are few, your loan system's module if you already run one, or a custom build for unusual borrowers[^35][^26][^47].
answers.own-data: Of the 12 vendors we checked, 5 state an accuracy figure, but none says how many documents it was measured on[^27][^28].
answers.rules: Lending rules require documented analysis and independent loan review, while model risk and vendor guidance cover the AI tool itself[^1][^2][^9][^5].
answers.benchmark: Run 20-50 files your analysts already signed through the tool, score each step against a double-keyed answer key, and trace every memo figure to a page[^40][^25].
answers.what-goes-wrong: AI spreads and memos go wrong through confident wrong numbers, untested accuracy claims, fake documents and rubber-stamped drafts[^22][^14][^20].
answers.buy-or-build: Buy spreading software if your template is standard, and build only when your own template and borrower mix are the edge[^48][^49].
answers.something-else: Pick something else if you close few deals, mostly spread simple returns, already own a loan system module, or need peer ratios more than faster keying[^25][^32][^50].
